subject: Startups
title: Customer Acquisition Cost
description: A short lesson to help you apply Customer Acquisition Cost.

hook.text: If it costs $500 to get a customer who pays you $100, you're not growing—you're burning.

buildup.text: CAC is total sales and marketing spend divided by the number of new customers acquired in that period.

discovery.text: A healthy SaaS business recovers CAC within 12–18 months. Faster payback means more capital for growth.

twist.text: CAC often rises as startups scale. The easiest customers come first. Later ones cost more to find and convert.

climax.text: The magic ratio is LTV:CAC of at least 3:1. Below that, growth costs more than the customer is worth.

punchline.text: Cheaper customers, faster payback. That's the growth engine.

quiz.question: What is the generally recommended LTV to CAC ratio?
